coupled_design.content_idea: The act of sharing tools makes different repairs one neighborhood experience. Build a relational graphic from actual repair contacts: two neighbors hold and tighten a wooden chair rail, another pair holds a shirt's torn seam and stitches it, two hands exchange a screwdriver, and lower contacts support a cloth patch and receive a spool. Their material continuities make the relation legible before any extra explanation.
coupled_design.distributed_graphic_execution: Give the upper-left chair a broad tilted back, two visible slats, a seat and a clear tightened rail. Two cuffed forearms end in distinct hands on the wood and driver. The center-upper contact is a substantial hand-to-hand screwdriver exchange. Upper right is a recognizable shirt with collar, sleeves and a jagged tear held open by two people; a needle actually meets the tear. Lower left returns to a jointly held chair structure, lower center shows a supported cloth patch, and lower right receives the same thread on a spool. Use meaningful changes of scale and angle among these contacts, with no card grid. The forearms, fingers and material/tool contact should feel human and specific, even in simplified ink shapes.
coupled_design.seam_and_crop_decisions: Reserve a broad opening through the middle as the information seam before shaping the surrounding graphic contacts. In the selected guide, a 1240x130 explanation block begins at x89,y413, below the invitation and between the upper object contours and lower supported objects. The upper wood brace points toward the invitation without crossing it. A sewing-thread connection bends around the right edge of the logistics and extends into the lower spool contact. These are physical continuities of the pictured repairs. The seam is open negative space within the full graphic field, with contours of real objects at its edges; its text is flat and unaffected by their perspective.
coupled_design.type_coupling: Place the medium-weight Korean title as an identity anchor over the upper-right shirt relation and the compact Latin phrase over the upper-left chair relation. The invitation sits at the left mouth of the seam and immediately opens the explanatory paragraph. Keep the paragraph as two complete sentence lines with a shared left start, generous body and natural spacing. The event name starts directly below the paragraph and opens a continuous horizontal name/date/time row. Venue, fee and deadline make the adjacent lower row, with URL under deadline at the right seam edge. The proposition belongs to the lower-left shared chair contact as the meaning of the work. Thus identity is paired with upper material relations, explanation spans their common seam, and action exits beside the real thread receiver.
coupled_design.material_color_emotion: Precisely drawn relational flat graphic with assertive angular cuts, real recognizable chair rails and fabric seams, dark green, acid yellow and warm vermilion against quiet paper. Bounded cut shapes and deliberate tool-contact geometry, not soft blob clipart or glossy props. Upper exchange and lower repair contacts are substantial linked image structures, not small corner decorations. Mature flat copy sits on the shared information seam; no fake fine print.
coupled_design.recognizable_visual_evidence: Chair structure with actual shared driver contact; shirt collar/sleeves and tear held by two hands; screwdriver passed from one clothed arm to another; cloth patch supported by a pair; thread connected to the lower-right hand and spool. These are linked experiences rather than interchangeable ornamental nodes.

reading_route.first_anchor: entry_01 together with the upper-right shirt's two-person stitch contact; entry_02 and the chair/tool transfer offer the complementary upper entry
reading_route.meaning_reprise: entry_03 sits over the lower-left jointly handled chair and closes the relational reading after the information seam.
reading_route.route_geometry: Upper-right identity to left seam mouth; stable two-line paragraph at x89; horizontal event row and immediately adjacent lower logistics row; down to URL at x1040. The lower-left proposition is attached to the lower chair contact, and the right thread carries the action exit to the spool.

guide.role: New coordinator-owned planning diagram for copy geometry and type anatomy; not a client asset, final style or fixed layout condition

common_constraints: Use the learned design ideas without fresh source-artwork searches or re-opening.
Design whole image and actual copy shape together. Every literal supplied entry appears once, with precise word spaces/punctuation and continuous mature body.
720px social display is a coordinator design assumption, not a fixed new client font/pixel/position rule.

Five whole organizations: continuous photographic scene/central spine; relational cut graphic/horizontal seam; edited photographic crop montage/offset title and sentence entry; expressive narrative column/flanking copy; full-height cut-print action/date-led side spine. These are current case choices, not runtime presets.

Own new guide refers to spatial relationships and exact type anatomy only. Convert placeholders into substantial current repair imagery; do not copy gray background, clipart figures or passive rectangles as the final style. No font-file-application promise.
Preserve native initial/repairs and close selection before critics. No quality scores by makers.

source_digest.case_entry_digest_method: UTF-8 canonical JSON, sorted keys, no extra whitespace

input_scope: One literal case/common input and one own role/direction; no corpus policies, peer plan or evaluation history.
